attributes.title: Learning Game
attributes.description: We explore people’s learning trajectories on a  novel visuomotor task.

comments.value:
*Hypothesis*
We hypothesize that, when learning a new skill, people’s learning progresses in accord with an exponential decay function (not linearly). Here, we will operationalize learning by tracking participant’s errors over time. We hypothesize that the rates of errors can be better described exponentially rather than linearly.

*Sample size*
We plan to collect data from 50 adult participants from Prolific. Participants will be excluded only based on the exclusion criterion (see below). Excluded participants will be replaced so that there are a total of 50 usable individuals.

*Exclusion criteria*
The learning task in this experiment demands a participant’s sustained attention over a period of 8 minutes (e.g., no switching between tabs, checking messages, or multitasking). We want to avoid participants not playing the game or paying attention. This is a particular problem when testing participants online vs. in well-controlled laboratory settings. In a previous pilot, we found 33% of participants didn’t show a positive learning slope. As we expect some rate of learning, and this task will be used to complement another study exploring people’s beliefs of learning, we plan to exclude participants who do not show any overall learning or improvement of the game.

For each participant, we plan to fit their performance errors over time during learning through a linear function: lm(trial_error ~ trial_no). If the coefficient is negative, the participant will be included in subsequent analyses. Otherwise, the participant will be excluded. 

We anticipate a moderately high exclusion rate given the features of this experiment. However, as explained above, the exclusion criteria helps us ensure that we will be analyzing data from participants who are learning the task of interest. 

For our secondary analyses, we will be run with both (1) a less stringent exclusion criteria and (2) a more strict exclusion with participants with statistically significant negative learning slopes (p<0.05) to allow for full exploration of the data and test the robustness of our exclusion criteria.
